children: According to Sina Finance, citing Gelonghui, several Wall Street institutions said the recent sell-off may be a correction within a bull market, rather than a clear sign of sustained deterioration in fundamentals.

Chris Larkin, head of trading at Morgan Stanley’s E*Trade, said the market move appeared to be driven mainly by sentiment, given that the economic and fundamental backdrop remained solid. Based on data through the current correction, the S&P 500 has fallen from a record high into correction territory 15 times since 1983; five of those declines eventually became bear markets, Larkin said.
Deutsche Bank analyst Binky Chadha said the market was “severely oversold,” while economic growth and corporate earnings remained strong.

title: Wall Street Institutions: Market May Be in a Bull-Market Correction
